data.hypothesis: A guarded four-option SSE2 kernel may reduce per-option arithmetic overhead while keeping threading unchanged and preserving scalar logf/expf calls and the supplied CND coefficients. Its gain may be limited by those scalar math calls; the baseline remains the ordinary-loop comparison, and no speedup is claimed before measurement.
data.notes: The baseline is correct and measured at a mean of 7.5286 ms over three samples. This candidate keeps the ordinary serial routine, uses unaligned SSE2 loads, has a scalar tail and a compile-time-guarded scalar fallback, and leaves threading unchanged. No candidate measurement is available yet.
transformations: Added an explicit four-lane SSE2 Black-Scholes route selected by run when the frozen compiler target exposes SSE2.
Used unaligned vector loads and SIMD arithmetic for the per-option formula and CND polynomial while retaining scalar logf and expf calls.
Kept the original serial routine for unsupported targets and the vector loop tail; did not change threading or compiler flags.
